"Act as a professional HTML5 game developer and educational game designer. You are an expert in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, animations, interactive game mechanics and user interface design.
GAME TITLE
[bacteria and archaea]
GAME CONCEPT
Create an exciting 3D-inspired adventure game similar to Roblox Obby Adventure, where players explore different environments, overcome obstacles and answer educational questions at every checkpoint.
The game must be educational, entertaining, interactive and suitable for students.
1. GAME INFORMATION
Title: [bacteria and archaea]
Genre: Educational Adventure / Obstacle Course / Quiz Game
Objective: Help players explore the game world, complete challenges, answer educational questions correctly and reach the final destination.
Theme: Colourful Roblox-inspired adventure world with cute cartoon-style characters, attractive environments and fun animations.
2. GAME STORYLINE
Create an interesting storyline with a beginning, middle and ending.
START – Introduction
Display an attractive welcome screen with the game title.
Introduce the main character and explain the mission.
Show a short storyline explaining why the player must complete all 15 checkpoints.
Include a START GAME button.
Include a HOW TO PLAY button.
MIDDLE – Adventure Journey
Players must travel through 15 different checkpoints.
Each checkpoint contains a unique obstacle or challenge.
Players must answer an educational question before unlocking the next checkpoint.
Questions should test the player's understanding of the selected educational topic.
Each checkpoint should have a different environment, design and challenge.
ENDING – Final Destination
After completing all 15 checkpoints, players reach the final destination.
Display a victory animation, fireworks and congratulatory messages.
Show the player's total score, number of correct answers and completion time.
Display a message such as \"Congratulations! You have completed your adventure!\"
Include a PLAY AGAIN button and a BACK TO MENU button.
3. GAME MECHANICS AND RULES
The player starts with 5 lives.
The initial score is 0.
There are exactly 15 checkpoints.
Every checkpoint contains at least one educational question.
Each correct answer awards 10 points.
Incorrect answers deduct 1 life.
Players must answer correctly to unlock the next checkpoint.
Players can retry a question if they answer incorrectly, as long as they have lives remaining.
Players cannot skip checkpoints.
Completing all 15 checkpoints means winning the game.
If all lives are lost, display the GAME OVER screen.
Include a progress bar showing checkpoint completion.
use this question and answer 
BIOLOGY: DOMAIN BACTERIA AND DOMAIN ARCHAEA

Question 1–5: Easy

1.Which of the following are the TWO domains of prokaryotes?

A. Bacteria and Fungi 
B. Bacteria and Archaea 
C. Archaea and Protista 
D. Bacteria and Plantae

2.Which bacterial cell shape is spherical?

A. Bacillus 
B. Vibrio 
C. Coccus 
D. Spirillum

3.Which of the following bacteria has a rod-shaped structure?

A. Bacillus 
B. Coccus 
C. Spirillum 
D. Vibrio

4.Which statement correctly describes prokaryotic cells?

A. They are multicellular organisms. 
B. They have a membrane-bound nucleus. 
C. They contain linear DNA inside the nucleus. 
D. They are unicellular organisms.

5.Which of the following is NOT a main type of Archaea based on habitat?

A. Methanogens 
B. Halophiles 
C. Thermoacidophiles 
D. Cyanobacteria

Question 6–10: Intermediate

6.Which bacterial cell shape is comma-shaped?

A. Spirillum 
B. Vibrio 
C. Bacillus 
D. Coccus

7.Which of the following bacteria is involved in nitrogen fixation?

A. Salmonella sp. 
B. E. coli 
C. Rhizobium sp. 
D. Vibrio cholerae

8.What is the main function of E. coli in the human intestine?

A. Causes food poisoning. 
B. Helps digestion and provides certain vitamins. 
C. Causes nitrogen fixation in humans. 
D. Produces toxins that cause diseases.

9.Which of the following is an example of pathogenic bacteria?

A. Rhizobium sp. 
B. E. coli 
C. Salmonella sp. 
D. Bacillus thuringiensis

Question 10 
Where is the genetic material of prokaryotic cells located?
A. Nucleus
B. Nucleoid region
C. Ribosome
D. Cytoplasm membrane

Question 11–15: Hard

11.A student observes a bacterium with a spiral-shaped structure under a microscope. Which bacterium could be observed?

A. Vibrio cholerae 
B. Rhodospirillum sp. 
C. E. coli 
D. Staphylococcus sp.

12.Which statement correctly explains nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium sp.?

A. Converts ammonia into atmospheric nitrogen. 
B. Converts atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia. 
C. Converts oxygen into nitrogen. 
D. Converts glucose into amino acids.

13.Which of the following is NOT a benefit of symbiotic bacteria in the human intestine?

A. Helps digest certain substances. 
B. Provides certain vitamins. 
C. Maintains a healthy balance in the gut.
D. Produces toxins that cause food poisoning.

14.In genetic engineering, how are bacterial plasmids used in biotechnology?

Question 14 
Which of the following products can be produced by genetically modified bacteria through genetic engineering?
A. Vitamins, antibiotics and hormones
B. Oxygen, glucose and water
C. Proteins, lipids and carbohydrates
D. Nitrogen, carbon dioxide and minerals

15.A scientist uses genetically modified bacteria to produce human insulin. Which process best describes this application?

A. Nitrogen fixation 
B. Symbiotic relationship 
C. Genetic engineering using recombinant plasmids 
D. Pathogenic infection

4. GAMEPLAY AND CHECKPOINT DESIGN
Create 15 unique checkpoints with different obstacles and environments.
Examples:
Forest Entrance – Introduce the first educational question.
Wooden Bridge – Jump across platforms.
Mystery Cave – Find the correct path.
River Crossing – Avoid moving obstacles.
Crystal Mountain – Climb platforms.
Lava Bridge – Jump between safe platforms.
Ice World – Navigate slippery platforms.
Hidden Temple – Solve a mystery question.
Sky Islands – Jump between floating islands.
Dark Forest – Find the correct direction.
Waterfall Challenge – Avoid moving obstacles.
Ancient Laboratory – Complete a science challenge.
Desert Adventure – Cross the desert.
Final Tower – Complete a difficult challenge.
Ultimate Destination – Answer the final question and win the game.
Each checkpoint must:
Have a unique name and environment.
Include an educational question.
Have three or four multiple-choice answers.
Display immediate feedback after answering.
Unlock the next checkpoint only after a correct answer.
5. QUESTION SYSTEM
Create an editable question bank in JavaScript.
Use this format:
{
question: \"Insert your question\",
answers: [\"Answer A\", \"Answer B\", \"Answer C\", \"Answer D\"],
correctAnswer: 1,
explanation: \"Explain why this answer is correct.\"
}
Requirements:
Support at least 15 questions.
Allow the developer to easily replace questions and answers.
Display one question at each checkpoint.
Randomise answer positions without changing the correct answer.
Display explanations after each answer.
Make the questions relevant to the selected educational topic.
6. HOW TO PLAY – GAME GUIDE
Create a separate HOW TO PLAY screen.
Desktop controls:
W / Arrow Up – Move forward.
S / Arrow Down – Move backward.
A / Arrow Left – Move left.
D / Arrow Right – Move right.
Spacebar – Jump.
Mobile controls:
Display an on-screen directional joystick or arrow buttons.
Add a dedicated jump button.
Ensure all controls work on touchscreens.
Game instructions:
Press START GAME.
Control your character and explore the environment.
Overcome obstacles to reach the checkpoint.
Answer the educational question.
Get the correct answer to unlock the next checkpoint.
Complete all 15 checkpoints to win!
7. VISUAL DESIGN AND FUN EFFECTS
Make the game visually attractive and exciting.
Include:
Bright pastel and vibrant colours.
Roblox-inspired cartoon environments.
Cute 3D-inspired characters.
Animated backgrounds.
Moving platforms and obstacles.
Collectible coins and stars.
Glowing checkpoint markers.
Animated question pop-up screens.
Confetti when answering correctly.
Red warning effects for incorrect answers.
Fireworks during the final victory.
Smooth transitions between checkpoints.
Background adventure music.
Sound effects for jumping, collecting coins, answering questions and winning.
Use CSS animations and JavaScript effects to make the game feel alive.
8. USER INTERFACE (UI)
The game must include these screens:
Start Screen – Game title, introduction and Start button.
How to Play Screen – Controls, rules and instructions.
Gameplay Screen – Character, environment, score, lives and progress.
Question Screen – Multiple-choice questions and answer feedback.
Checkpoint Screen – Display checkpoint completion.
Game Over Screen – Final score and retry option.
Victory Screen – Celebration after completing all 15 checkpoints.
Display the following during gameplay:
Current score.
Remaining lives.
Current checkpoint (e.g. 5/15).
Progress bar.
Pause and Resume buttons.
9. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Create the complete game using:
HTML5 for structure.
CSS3 for design, animations and visual effects.
JavaScript for gameplay, movement, questions, scoring and interactions.
IMPORTANT:
Put all HTML, CSS and JavaScript in ONE single HTML file.
Do not require external files or paid libraries.
The game must work by opening the HTML file in a web browser.
Ensure compatibility with desktop and mobile devices.
All buttons and game controls must function correctly.
Make sure all 15 checkpoints are playable.
Include a complete beginning, gameplay journey and ending.
Write clean, organised and commented code.
Do not leave incomplete functions or placeholder gameplay.
FINAL INSTRUCTION
Generate the FULL, COMPLETE and PLAYABLE HTML CODE.
Do not provide only a game description or prototype. Build the actual interactive educational adventure game with all 15 checkpoints, questions, obstacles, controls, animations, scoring system, start screen and victory ending.
The final output must be a single HTML file that can be saved as index.html and opened directly in Chrome.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs

Network:

  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:

Global options:

It includes all 15 checkpoints and biology questions, randomized answer choices, movement and jumping, obstacles and collectibles, lives and scoring, touch controls, pause and guide screens, generated music and sound effects, and game-over and victory screens.

**Checks:** HTML parsing and JavaScript syntax passed; confirmed 15 questions and 15 checkpoints. I couldn’t capture a browser screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in the environment.
